title: Introduce tasklet-driven batcher and remove KV read hotpath contention
creator: Amira Gonzalez
description: Refactor the continuous batching and KV cache read path by replacing the coarse-grained thread-affinity scheduler with a tasklet-driven batcher and an epoched KV read snapshot. Goal is to reduce contention on KV readers, remove tail latency spikes caused by worker handoffs, and make the admission path lock-free for steady-state traffic.
background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated multiple tactical changes to the batcher and KV cache to handle bursty traffic and heterogeneous model sizes. These patches rely on thread-affinity, spinlocks around shard maps, and per-request handoff queues that cause tail latency regressions during GC and hotkey storms. Previous tickets (see dependencies) attempted piecemeal fixes. This ticket scopes a more structural change: move to lightweight tasklets (cooperative micro-tasks) scheduled on a small worker pool and introduce an epoched read snapshot for KV to avoid long-lived locks during reads.
decision_log: 2025-01-15: Decided to adopt a tasklet abstraction rather than full async/await migration to keep change surface small.
2025-01-22: Chosen epoched KV snapshot approach over copy-on-write because it has lower steady-state overhead for our read-dominant workload.
2025-02-03: Keep legacy scheduler as a fallback behind a runtime flag for canary rollouts (runtime.enable_tasklet_batcher).
2025-02-10: Upgrade third-party concurrency library to folly 2025.01 as part of this change; security review completed (see links).
implementation_plan: Introduce tasklet scheduler module with bounded work queues and per-worker cooperative yield points.
Refactor batcher to emit tasklets for request admission and batching windows instead of thread handoff queues.
Implement epoched KV snapshot: writers bump epoch; readers read current epoch pointer and use lock-free reads against immutable segment pointers.
Add metrics and tracing for tasklet queue depth, epoch churn, kvcache-read-latency, and legacy_fallback_count.
Add runtime flags and feature gate: runtime.enable_tasklet_batcher, runtime.kv_epoch_debug=true/false.
Write unit and integration tests covering concurrency scenarios and KV snapshot visibility guarantees.
Build a canary deployment and gradual ramp strategy with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
migration_steps: 1) Merge tasklet scheduler behind feature flag; keep legacy scheduler as default.
2) Deploy to canary fleet (5% of traffic) with synthetic load and production-like prompt sets.
3) Monitor p50/p95/p99 generation latency, CPU, and token cost. Run A/B traffic split for 24 hours.
4) If stable, ramp feature to 25% then 60% then 100%; at each step run smoke tests and automated SLO checks.
5) Once at 100%, remove legacy code paths and clean up runtime flags in follow-up cleanup ticket.
acceptance_criteria: p99 inference latency for short-sequence generation (<=128 tokens) improves by at least 15% on average in synthetic and replayed workloads compared to baseline.
Observed KV read contention (lock hold time) reduced by >60% under hotkey replication test.
No increase in per-token CPU cost beyond 5% in steady-state traffic.
All new metrics emitted and dashboards created; alerting added for tasklet-queue-depth > 200 sustained for 5m.
Canary rollouts succeed with zero customer-facing errors and automatic rollback triggers validated.
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Spike implementation completed for tasklet scheduler (prototype in experimental/tasklet). Basic bench shows lower tail latency under synthetic burst.
2025-01-28: Completed epoched KV snapshot PoC; microbench shows read latency stable under concurrent writer load.
2025-02-05: Integrated batcher with tasklet scheduler; initial unit tests passing. Found race when shutting down workers — added cooperative drain flow.
2025-02-12: End-to-end integration tests flaked in CI due to dependency on folly upgrade; PR #7882 opened to pin new library ABI.
2025-02-20: Canary deployment targeted for 2025-02-25 after completing PR reviews and adding observability panels.
testing_plan: Unit tests for tasklet scheduling semantics (yield, preemption, cancellation).
Stress tests with synthetic hotkey traffic to verify KV epoch correctness and read isolation.
Replay tests using production traffic capture to validate latency improvements and no semantic regressions.
Chaos test: worker process kill during a batching window to ensure graceful fallback to legacy scheduler and no request loss.
Performance regression tests in CI comparing p50/p95/p99 against baseline artifacts.
rollout_plan: Canary in us-east-1 (5% traffic) for 24h with automated SLO checks.
If pass, ramp to 25% for 48h and re-run A/B analysis.
50%+ ramp only if CPU/tokens cost remain within target and error rate stays flat.
Full rollout and immediate cleanup of legacy scheduler within two sprints post-rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: New scheduler might interact poorly with GPU preemption and cause uneven batching -> Mitigation: Add back-pressure signal from GPU workers and limit tasklet creation rate.
Risk: Epoched snapshot increases memory due to short-lived immutable segments -> Mitigation: Add segment compaction policy and monitor mem-growth metrics.
Risk: Folly upgrade could cause ABI or test flakiness -> Mitigation: Run extended CI matrix and coordinate runtime dependency owners.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids touching public API surface (no client-visible changes). Follow-up cleanup ticket will delete legacy scheduler and remove runtime flags. Coordinate on-call for rollout windows and ensure runbooks are updated.
